candidateAnalysis.currentStatus: historical assessment; continuation to September unresolved
candidateAnalysis.assessment: Transitional dependence in existing Claude-enabled classified operational assistance: substitution required a managed transition while operations continued. No permanent irreplaceability, precise cost or provider remote veto established.
candidateAnalysis.construct: Reliance on a provider-specific capability in an existing operational function where immediate withdrawal is constrained by maintaining that function during replacement. This permits alternatives and divided technical control.
candidateAnalysis.rubricChangeRationale: Separate transition-constrained product dependence from dependence on an ongoing service or remote provider control. This distinction applies symmetrically to any supplier, including offline deployed systems; it is not a relaxation of evidence requirements or a claim that all purchases create dependence.

necessaryConditions.reason: Government confirms active operations; supplier narrows functional context to intelligence/planning assistance, with court corroboration of defence deployment. Not a claim that Claude independently selects targets.

Named Anthropic models remain the deployed capability; development/provision/licensing differs from customer control of static copies. Ongoing remote provider control is not required for product dependence.

Active use persisted after the removal decision; responsible CIO links transition time and exceptions to operational continuity; phased licenses/support and government single-provider characterization corroborate constraint. No exact minimum duration or dollar cost inferred.
Assessment dated March24 for ongoing classified operational assistance; later alternatives prevent extending the finding automatically to September.

Interoperability, prospective low disruption and alternative agreements rebut permanent irreplaceability, not transitional constraint. Frozen deployed models limit provider veto; they do not make model-specific workflows instantly replaceable.

candidateAnalysis.sufficientRule: All five conditions supported, with government operational-continuity evidence and a distinct instrument or deployment record. Announced procurement, continued use alone, or a phase-out deadline alone is insufficient.
candidateAnalysis.necessityResult: supported for dated transitional construct; permanent/structural dependence not assessed as established
candidateAnalysis.sufficiencyResult: candidate supported qualitative inference; root substantive review required before canonical coding or publication
notEstablished: No viable substitute under every feasible operational adjustment
Continuing need for Anthropic engineers or new model versions
candidateAnalysis.counterEvidenceTreatment: Alternatives may exist yet need validated integration. March optimism is recorded as conflicting expectation, while later agreements and frozen copies limit scope. Unnamed contractor costs are not used to satisfy the condition for named military functions.
limitations: The government confirms operational use without a public workflow-by-workflow inventory. Intelligence/planning description comes from the supplier.
No observed instantaneous removal counterfactual. The inference relies on responsible agency explanation that managed transition protects ongoing operations.
Assessment has no ordinal intensity; substantial or mission-structural dependence is not established.
March24 statement does not show whether an exemption was ever granted or migration completed.

fallbackFindings.assessment: Supported: supplier model provision and customer/cloud operational approval are consequential distinct controls.
Supported historical reliance, now independently corroborated by CIO operational testimony; exact essentiality and task-level intensity remain unmeasured.
